THESE RIDE IN EVERY PROMPT. They are data, not documentation, so an
editor adding a thirteenth item cannot forget them: the renderer appends
`rules_clause` to every positive prompt and refuses to build a prompt
that does not carry it (imagegen.py: build_prompt / _selftest_rules).
WHY: every 1980s British advert, poster and packet is still in copyright
for decades yet, and trade mark was the ONLY claim Getty actually won in
[2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch). A model asked for `a British high street in 1989`
will happily paint a real brewery's livery on a pub. So we never ask for
one. In-world brands only, which is better content anyway - MICKEY'S is
a place in this game and a real brewery is not.
AND THIS IS THE ONE CLAUSE THAT STAYS IN THE POSITIVE PROMPT, 25 Aug.
Every other exclusion moved to `negatives` below. This one did not, and
the reason is measured rather than cautious: sd-cli only evaluates the
unconditional branch when cfg != 1.0 (see `negatives._comment`), and this
batch runs at cfg 1.0 because Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for it. A
negative prompt is therefore INERT here - so moving the anti-brand,
anti-real-person clause into it would have deleted the only instruction
the model actually receives on the subject. It is mirrored into the
negative as well, where it will start acting the day an item raises cfg.
The exclusion scan in imagegen.py exempts this clause BY NAME and prints
that it did, so the hole is a line of output rather than a silence.
D18, 2026-09-10. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS CLAUSE IS THE CONTENT RULE,
recorded at ledger-v2/respec/decision-register/D18-content-rule.md and in
canon.md. Alcohol and gambling out entirely; nobody under eighteen and no
school in use; nothing sexual. Tobacco, violence and period swearing STAY

THE CLAUSE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS EVERY PROMPT-BEARING SPEC and that is
now CHECKED rather than hoped for: tools/content-gate.py compares all of
them against each other and against the token list, and refuses the run if
one drifts. Before that check existed, three of these files carried a

WHY THE ABSTRACT WORDS INSTRUCT AND THE CONCRETE WORDS REFUSE. This clause
rides in the POSITIVE prompt and validate_spec scans that composed prompt
against forbidden_tokens. So the clause says `no alcohol` and the tokens
say `beer`: a token list containing its own clause's words would refuse
every item in the library. Measured, not assumed. The first wording said
`nothing served or drunk` and the token `drunk` inside it would have done
exactly that; the gate's selftest caught it before it shipped.

items.prompt: A concept sheet for THE PARADE, the nightlife district of Meridian, a fictional British port town, at ten to eleven at night in 1990. Two stacked photoreal panels inside a pale paper border: top an orientation view along the street, bottom the same street at standing eye height. TOP: from the middle of the wet carriageway at 1.6 m, looking north along Tivoli Street, a terrace of nine narrow shop units under a black sky. The cinema fills the left third: a 1928 picture house with a flat canopy over the pavement carrying a row of small round lamps, three of them dark, and three lit poster cases in the recessed entrance. Beside it a fish and chip shop whose window is running with condensation and whose fluorescent light throws a hard white pool three metres out across the wet flagstones. Then a video rental shop lit by cold strip lights with shelves of cases facing the glass, a hall doorway with a bill wall forty layers deep beside it, an all-night cafe with steam on the inside of the window, an amusement shopfront where the only moving light in the picture comes from the screens of upright cabinets, a dark chemist, a launderette lit flat and cold and empty, and one entirely dark unit at the end. Sodium street lamps overhead make everything orange above head height and the shop windows make everything white and warm below it. Every surface is wet and every light is doubled in the road. everything on every sign and in every window is food, film, music, laundry, medicine or a telephone number, and every person in the picture is an adult. BOTTOM: camera at 1.6 m on the pavement between the cinema and the chip shop, close enough to touch the wall. A queue of eleven adults in ordinary British clothes of 1990 stands along the chip shop window in the wet, collars up, silent, each of them facing the window. On the brick wall at 1.4 m a black telephone handset in a steel hood, its face plain where a dial would be, and a small painted card above it, and a man with his back to the camera holding the handset. Behind him the cinema canopy lamps, a red public telephone box with three people at it and one holding the door open with a foot, a cast iron street lamp, a pillar box, and four saloon cars nose to tail at the kerb with their side lights on and exhaust condensing. Wet flagstones, a running gutter, chip papers in the channel, cigarette ends, a puddle across the whole foreground with the cinema lamps in it. Overcast, moonless, rain just stopped. EXACTLY THREE PIECES OF LETTERING IN THE WHOLE SHEET: the title PARADE, the small subtitle CONCEPT PROPOSAL, and the cinema fascia reading TIVOLI in raised capitals; each crisp and correctly spelled, and every other fascia, card, poster and window in the sheet is a plain unlettered painted board or an even block of texture. Two small rows along the bottom of the sheet: an upper row of four flat material swatches, pale glazed wall tile, dark oxblood vinyl, cream painted stucco, warm orange neon tube; below it three objects against the paper border, a rope on two posts, a lit poster case, and a black telephone handset in a steel hood. Both rows plain and unlabelled. Photoreal throughout, everything period-correct for 1990. A proposal drawn for review.

items._negative_note: AT cfg 1.0 THIS IS NEVER EVALUATED, and the tool prints that in its own words. IT ALSO NO LONGER NAMES THE THINGS D17 BARS, and that is a correction the tool forced rather than a choice: check_forbidden scans the positive AND the negative together and refused this spec for naming four of them in the veto half. The tool is right and the reason is the same one that governs the whole file: at cfg 1.0 a veto does nothing, so the only protection that works is the positive clause, and writing the banned nouns anywhere is a risk with no benefit.

acceptance: OPEN THE IMAGE. A green exit code is not acceptance and neither is a file existing.
Read at 100 percent: are the three strings correct and correctly spelled, and is every other surface unlettered? Count the letterings and print the count.
Is any sign, window, glass, pump, bottle, machine or poster in the frame drink or a wager? IF ONE IS, THE SHEET IS REFUSED, whatever else it does well. Print the count examined, not just the finding.
Is it wet, overcast and at night, per canon's Tone?
Is the bottom panel at standing eye height and outdoors?
